correctness.rationale: The finite domain is exhaustive. The verifier derives all minimal recovery sets directly from the \(3\times 8\) binary generator matrix and obtains 11 for each request. With \(L=2\), any selected service has multiplicity at most two because it intersects every copy of itself. Hence all possibilities lie in \(3^{11}\) multiplicity vectors per request. Exact integer/set enumeration leaves 141 same-request-feasible candidates per request, 306 mutually compatible candidate pairs for each request pair, and exactly two global triples; direct decoding yields the two claimed multisets and shows all three request totals equal five.

value.rationale: The matrix is the paper's canonical example establishing that multiset services genuinely enlarge the newly introduced recovery model. Classifying the exact \((5,2)\) solution space is therefore a natural boundary invariant rather than an arbitrary slice: it shows strong rigidity, proves that the paper's construction is one of only two labeled possibilities, and identifies the only missing witness. This gives a reproducible finite benchmark for understanding and testing the new service-multiset formalism.
